- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) and model forecast is flat or rising slowly, adjust upward by 2–5% to account for sentiment-driven momentum.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior period), model tends to overcorrect; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% for next 5–7 days.  
- If official supply net is negative and sentiment is bearish, model often underestimates downside; add 3–8% downward bias to forecast mean.  
- When sentiment swings from bullish to bearish within 3–5 days, model often fails to adjust; apply a 5–10% downward correction to forecast mean.  
- In high-event periods (≥18 events/30d), model tends to overestimate volatility; cap forecast range within ±3% of recent 7-day moving average.  
- If model forecast is flat or trending upward while true outcome shows mean reversion, reduce forecast slope by 15–25% for next 3–5 days.  
- When sentiment is negative and supply net is negative, model often ignores policy impact; add 5–10% downward bias to forecast mean.
